  Problem: The memo function is invoked by both callers via `declare -F _autofix_review_default_branch_prime >/dev/null && _autofix_review_default_branch_prime` (lines 1603, 1816), and it is also re-invoked at the top of every `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs` call via the `else` branch when no memo is present. The two-callers-in-same-step scenario is the primary motivation. However, any other future caller of `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs` that runs in the same step shell as either of these two callers (and does not itself call the prime) will inherit the memo and consume a value the prime caller established — which is exactly the intended cross-caller reuse. There is no actual defect here; the call is documented and the design is sound.
  Why it fails at runtime: This is a NIT, not a defect — memo reuse across same-shell callers is the design goal. No runtime failure path identified.
